Declared: Retrieves recommendations from AWS Compute Optimizer.

Args:
    ctx: The MCP context
    operation: The operation to perform (e.g., 'get_ec2_instance_recommendations')
    region: AWS region to query (e.g., 'us-west-2'). Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or us-east-1.
    max_items: Total number of items to return across all pages. Omit it to fetch
        every page.
    filters: Optional filter expression as JSON string
    account_ids: Optional JSON array with a single AWS account ID, e.g. '["123456789012"]',
        or the bare ID
    next_token: The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with
        otherwise identical parameters.
    resource_arns: Optional JSON array of resource ARNs to return recommendations for
    order_by: get_idle_recommendations only. Optional JSON object
        {"dimension": "SavingsValue"|"SavingsValueAfterDiscount", "order": "Asc"|"Desc"};
        defaults to SavingsValueAfterDiscount, Desc
    cpu_vendor_architectures: EC2, Auto Scaling group, and RDS only. Optional JSON
        array of CURRENT and/or AWS_ARM64, sent as
        recommendationPreferences.cpuVendorArchitectures; the API defaults to CURRENT

Returns:
    Dict containing the Compute Optimizer recommendations | Detected: environment_access

new_findings.title: MCP Capability Mismatch: file_access
new_findings.evidence:
Declared: Validate SQL for Aurora DSQL compatibility and optionally auto-fix issues.

Parses SQL and reports compatibility errors (unsupported syntax) with suggested fixes.
Use fix=True to generate DSQL-compatible SQL automatically.

## When to Use
- Before executing any externally-sourced SQL (ORM migrations, pg_dump, hand-written DDL)
- When migrating schemas from PostgreSQL, MySQL, or other databases to DSQL
- To validate CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and other DDL statements
- To check transaction structure (DSQL requires one DDL per transaction)

## Fix Behavior
When fix=True, each diagnostic carries a `fix_result.status`:
- `fixed`: safe mechanical transformation applied
- `fixed_with_warning`: fix applied but may require application code changes
- unfixable diagnostics have no `fix_result` and require manual intervention | Detected: file_access
new_findings.remediation: Update tool description or restrict source code permissions.

Declared: Retrieves recommendations from AWS Compute Optimizer.

Args:
    ctx: The MCP context
    operation: The operation to perform (e.g., 'get_ec2_instance_recommendations')
    region: AWS region to query (e.g., 'us-west-2'). Defaults to AWS_REGION env var or us-east-1.
    max_items: Total number of items to return across all pages. Omit it to fetch
        every page.
    filters: Optional filter expression as JSON string
    account_ids: Optional JSON array with a single AWS account ID, e.g. '["123456789012"]',
        or the bare ID
    next_token: The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with
        otherwise identical parameters.
    resource_arns: Optional JSON array of resource ARNs to return recommendations for
    order_by: get_idle_recommendations only. Optional JSON object
        {"dimension": "SavingsValue"|"SavingsValueAfterDiscount", "order": "Asc"|"Desc"};
        defaults to SavingsValueAfterDiscount, Desc
    cpu_vendor_architectures: EC2, Auto Scaling group, and RDS only. Optional JSON
        array of CURRENT and/or AWS_ARM64, sent as
        recommendationPreferences.cpuVendorArchitectures; the API defaults to CURRENT

Returns:
    Dict containing the Compute Optimizer recommendations | Detected: environment_access

findings.title: MCP Capability Mismatch: file_access
findings.evidence:
Declared: Validate SQL for Aurora DSQL compatibility and optionally auto-fix issues.

Parses SQL and reports compatibility errors (unsupported syntax) with suggested fixes.
Use fix=True to generate DSQL-compatible SQL automatically.

## When to Use
- Before executing any externally-sourced SQL (ORM migrations, pg_dump, hand-written DDL)
- When migrating schemas from PostgreSQL, MySQL, or other databases to DSQL
- To validate CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and other DDL statements
- To check transaction structure (DSQL requires one DDL per transaction)

## Fix Behavior
When fix=True, each diagnostic carries a `fix_result.status`:
- `fixed`: safe mechanical transformation applied
- `fixed_with_warning`: fix applied but may require application code changes
- unfixable diagnostics have no `fix_result` and require manual intervention | Detected: file_access
findings.remediation: Update tool description or restrict source code permissions.

new_findings.title: Likely Test/Example Data: Exposed PEM Private Key Block
new_findings.description: Hardcoded PEM Private Key Block detected in source file.
new_findings.remediation: Verify whether this test fixture contains mock data. If intentionally mock, annotate with '# pragma: allowlist secret' or '# nosec'.

new_findings.title: Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution (eval/exec)
new_findings.description: Use of eval() / exec() can lead to arbitrary code execution if dynamic or AI-generated input reaches it.
new_findings.remediation: Avoid dynamic code execution. Use safe JSON parsers or declarative dispatcher tables.

new_findings.title: Container Running as Root / Sensitive Port Exposed
new_findings.description: Dockerfile explicitly sets root user or exposes administrative ports (SSH, Docker Daemon, Redis, MongoDB) without non-root privilege drop.
new_findings.remediation: Create and switch to a dedicated non-root user (e.g. USER appuser) and avoid exposing raw internal database/management ports in containers.

new_findings.title: Likely Test/Example Data: Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution (eval/exec)
new_findings.description: Use of eval() / exec() can lead to arbitrary code execution if dynamic or AI-generated input reaches it.
new_findings.remediation: Verify whether this test fixture contains mock data. If intentionally mock, annotate with '# pragma: allowlist secret' or '# nosec'.

new_findings.title: Potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
new_findings.description: Server-side HTTP request made directly to a dynamic, user-supplied URL without destination validation, enabling SSRF attacks against internal services or cloud metadata.
new_findings.remediation: Validate destination URLs against an explicit allowlist of authorized domains and restrict internal IP/localhost resolution.

new_findings.title: Secret Interpolated Directly in CI/CD Shell Script
new_findings.description: GitHub Actions secrets interpolated directly into `run:` scripts are vulnerable to command injection and process argument inspection.
new_findings.evidence:
run:
#   gh aw compile
# Not all edits will cause changes to this file.
#
# For more information: https://github.github.com/gh-aw/introducti
new_findings.remediation: Pass secrets as environment variables (`env: SECRET_VAL: ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}`) and reference them via shell `$SECRET_VAL`.

timeline.title: New MEDIUM Risk Detected: Retrieved from Cache
timeline.details: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.

timeline.title: New MEDIUM Risk Detected: Re-examine Cache-control Directives
timeline.details: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached.

timeline.title: New MEDIUM Risk Detected: Modern Web Application
timeline.details: The application appears to be a modern web application. If you need to explore it automatically then the Ajax Spider may well be more effective than the standard one.

timeline.title: New LOW Risk Detected: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
timeline.details: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.

timeline.title: New LOW Risk Detected: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
timeline.details: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797.

timeline.title: New LOW Risk Detected: HTTPS Content Available via HTTP
timeline.details: Content which was initially accessed via HTTPS (i.e.: using SSL/TLS encryption) is also accessible via HTTP (without encryption).

timeline.title: New MEDIUM Risk Detected: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
timeline.details: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

new_findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
new_findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.
new_findings.evidence: Reported by OWASP ZAP DAST engine
new_findings.remediation:
Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.

new_findings.title: Retrieved from Cache
new_findings.description: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.
new_findings.evidence: Reported by OWASP ZAP DAST engine
new_findings.remediation:
Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user:

Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private

Pragma: no-cache

Expires: 0

This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.

Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.
findings.scanner_evidence: Reported by OWASP ZAP DAST engine
findings.technical_explanation: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.
findings.business_impact: Potential operational, configuration, or compliance degradation.

findings.title: Retrieved from Cache
findings.description: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.
findings.evidence: Reported by OWASP ZAP DAST engine
findings.remediation:
Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user:

Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private

Pragma: no-cache

Expires: 0

This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.

metadata.name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 & DPDP Rules, 2025 (India)
metadata.authority: Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
metadata.version: DPDP Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023) & DPDP Rules, 2025
metadata.description: Comprehensive statutory framework governing the processing of digital personal data in India. Establishes legal accountability for Data Fiduciaries, statutory safeguards, breach notification, and Data Principal rights.
metadata.disclaimer: TrustAudit provides automated technical gap analysis, evidence tracking, and readiness evaluation. It does not replace formal legal counsel or statutory audit by DPBI. TrustAudit is not a registered statutory Consent Manager under Section 6(9).

commencement_timeline.consent_managers_in_force: Section 6(9) & Rule 4 (Registration and operation of Consent Managers) commenced on 13 November 2026.
commencement_timeline.substantive_fiduciary_scheduled: Substantive Data Fiduciary obligations (including Sections 5, 8, 9, 10) and Rules 3, 5–16 are scheduled to commence on 13 May 2027.
commencement_timeline.status_distinction: Delineates controls as: Already in force, Scheduled to commence, Readiness assessment, Not applicable, or Requires legal review. Future statutory requirements are assessed for preparedness and never represented as existing legal violations.

controls.title: Notice-Related Requirements for Data Processing
controls.official_ref: DPDP Act 2023, Section 5 read with DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 3
controls.description: Every request for consent must be accompanied or preceded by an itemised notice informing the Data Principal of the personal data to be processed, specified purpose, manner of exercising rights, and grievance redressal mechanism.
controls.rationale: Technical checks passed and 10 supporting evidence document(s) uploaded.
assessment_questions: Does your website or application present an itemized notice before capturing user personal data?
Is the notice accessible in English and any of the 22 languages specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India?
Does the notice explicitly explain how users can withdraw consent or raise a grievance?
evidence_requirements: Screenshot / URL of current Privacy Notice and Consent banner.
Copy of multilingual consent notice texts.
Application log format demonstrating notice version presented before consent.
recommended_actions: Deploy an itemized consent banner that lists each data category and specific purpose separately.
Provide direct links to grievance officer details in the notice text.

controls.title: Consent Architecture & Consent Manager Integration
controls.official_ref: DPDP Act 2023, Section 6(9) read with DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 4
controls.description: Data Principals may give, manage, review, or withdraw consent through registered Consent Managers accountable to the DPBI. TrustAudit tracks organizational technical readiness to interface with registered Consent Managers and does not self-attest as a registered Consent Manager.
controls.rationale: Technical scanner checks passed with 0 related vulnerabilities, but formal policy or audit document has not yet been uploaded to Evidence Vault.
assessment_questions: Can users withdraw their consent easily via account settings with equal ease to giving consent?
Is your data architecture prepared to process standard interoperable consent tokens from registered Consent Managers?
evidence_requirements: Documentation or UI workflow showing the self-service consent withdrawal flow.
Consent lifecycle database schema or audit trail format.
recommended_actions: Implement a dedicated 'Manage Privacy Preferences' portal in user dashboard.
Ensure withdrawal of consent cascades downstream to data processors and third-party vendors.

controls.title: General Data Fiduciary Responsibility
controls.description: A Data Fiduciary shall be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.
controls.rationale: 26 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Has your organization established formal data governance policies covering processors acting on your behalf?
Do Data Processor contracts mandate strict compliance with DPDP standards?
evidence_requirements: Data Protection Governance Charter.
Standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) executed with third-party vendors.
recommended_actions: Execute Data Processing Addenda with all cloud and SaaS vendors handling user personal data.
Designate an executive lead accountable for personal data processing compliance.

controls.title: Technical and Organisational Measures
controls.description: A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.
controls.rationale: Technical scanner checks passed with 0 related vulnerabilities, but formal policy or audit document has not yet been uploaded to Evidence Vault.
assessment_questions: Are role-based access controls (RBAC) and least privilege enforced across internal databases?
Are regular automated security assessments, dependency audits, and SAST scans embedded in CI/CD?
evidence_requirements: Access control policy and quarterly privilege review records.
TrustAudit automated CI/CD security audit reports.
recommended_actions: Enforce multi-tenant access controls and least-privilege scoping across all database queries.
Embed TrustAudit automated PR security checks in build pipelines.

controls.title: Reasonable Security Safeguards to Prevent Personal Data Breach
controls.official_ref: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(5) read with DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 6
controls.description: A Data Fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession or under its control by taking reasonable security safeguards including encryption, secret protection, perimeter defense, and vulnerability patching to prevent personal data breach.
controls.effective_date: 13 May 2027 (Scheduled commencement; IT Act Section 43A baseline in force)
controls.rationale: 218 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are all production credentials, database passwords, and API keys excluded from repositories and stored in secure key vaults?
Is all personal data encrypted in transit using modern TLS (1.2/1.3) with HSTS enforced?
Are automated vulnerability scans conducted regularly across repositories, APIs, and web perimeters?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit Secret Detection report confirming 0 active exposed production secrets.
TLS certificate verification and perimeter security header audit report.
Data-at-rest and in-transit encryption architecture documentation.
recommended_actions: Revoke and rotate any hardcoded credentials detected in source code.
Enforce HTTPS with HSTS on all personal-data-ingesting endpoints.

controls.title: Intimation of Personal Data Breach to DPBI & Data Principals
controls.official_ref: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(6) read with DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 7
controls.description: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Data Protection Board of India and each affected Data Principal intimation in such form, manner, and time as prescribed under Rule 7.
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Do you maintain an active Incident Response Plan with defined DPBI breach notification procedures?
Can your system identify which users' personal data was accessed or compromised within 24 hours of breach detection?
evidence_requirements: Incident Response Policy document detailing DPBI reporting thresholds and templates.
Breach drill / tabletop simulation report from past 12 months.
recommended_actions: Establish automated alert rules for anomalous credential dumps or data exfiltration attempts.
Draft pre-approved notification templates for Data Principals and DPBI.

controls.title: Data Erasure and Purpose Limitation
controls.description: A Data Fiduciary must erase personal data upon consent withdrawal or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose for which personal data was collected is no longer being served, unless retention is required by law.
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Do you have an automated data retention and scheduled purging mechanism for inactive or deleted accounts?
Are backup archives purged or sanitized according to retention limits?
evidence_requirements: Data Retention & Erasure Schedule policy.
Database cron / cleanup script configuration logs demonstrating periodic erasure.
recommended_actions: Define explicit retention timeframes per data category (e.g. 180 days post-account closure).
Implement database soft-deletion followed by permanent hard-purge.

controls.title: Processing of Personal Data of Children
controls.official_ref: DPDP Act 2023, Section 9 read with applicable DPDP Rules 2025
controls.description: A Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing personal data of a child. Must not undertake tracking or behavioral monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children.
controls.rationale: Excluded based on business profile: organization does not offer goods or services directed at minors.
assessment_questions: Do your products or AI tools process personal data of individuals under 18 years of age?
If applicable, is verifiable parental consent obtained prior to account creation?
Are tracking cookies and behavioral profiling scripts disabled for child accounts?
evidence_requirements: Age-gating verification flow screenshots or code logic.
Parental consent verification mechanism documentation.
recommended_actions: Implement age verification gate at onboarding.
Disable all tracking cookies and analytics pixels for accounts registered to minors.

controls.title: Additional Obligations of Significant Data Fiduciaries (SDF)
controls.description: Central Government may notify any Data Fiduciary as SDF based on volume, sensitivity, and risk. SDFs must appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India, an independent data auditor, and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA).
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Has your organization evaluated whether its user base or data volume meets SDF classification criteria?
Have you appointed a Data Protection Officer (DPO) based in India?
Do you conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA)?
evidence_requirements: DPO appointment letter and public contact details.
Latest Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) report.
recommended_actions: Designate an India-based DPO with direct reporting to the Board.
Establish annual third-party security and privacy audit schedule.

metadata.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
metadata.authority: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
metadata.version: 2017 TSC with 2022 Points of Focus (Published Criteria)
metadata.description: AICPA Trust Services Criteria ensuring service organizations establish rigorous technical and operational controls across Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy.
metadata.disclaimer: SOC 2 tracking in TrustAudit represents readiness evaluation and evidence management. Automated mappings cover selected technical criteria and do not constitute complete SOC 2 coverage, an issued SOC 2 examination report, or CPA attestation.

controls.title: Logical Access Security
controls.description: The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security events.
controls.rationale: 26 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are all repository secrets, API keys, and database passwords excluded from source code and managed via dedicated secret stores?
Is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) strictly enforced for all developer accounts, cloud consoles, and Git repositories?
Are user access permissions reviewed on at least a quarterly basis?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit automated Secret Scan report demonstrating 0 active exposed keys.
MFA enforcement screenshots from identity provider (Okta/Google Workspace/GitHub).
Quarterly access review sign-off sheets.
recommended_actions: Remove and rotate any hardcoded API keys detected in codebases.
Enforce GitHub organization-wide MFA and signed commits.

controls.title: Protection Against Threats Originating Outside System Boundaries
controls.description: The entity implements logical boundaries and network protections against threats originating outside system boundaries.
controls.rationale: 31 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Is all network traffic to web applications encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with strong cipher suites?
Are modern HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options) properly configured on public perimeter endpoints?
Are internal debug, actuator, or swagger interfaces restricted from unauthenticated public exposure?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit Website Perimeter & TLS Analysis report.
Cloud firewall / security group configuration export showing restricted ingress ports.
recommended_actions: Enable HSTS with minimum 1-year max-age on production domains.
Restrict administrative API endpoints behind private VPN or IP allowlists.

controls.title: Prevention, Detection, and Remediation of Unauthorised or Malicious Software
controls.description: The entity implements controls to prevent, detect, and remediate the introduction of unauthorized software, malicious code, or compromised agent integrations.
controls.rationale: 135 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Do all AI agents and MCP tools operate under least-privilege permission boundaries?
Are MCP tools audited for description mismatch, prompt injection poisoning, and typosquatted dependencies?
Is runtime firewalling or execution approval enforced before AI agents run system shell commands?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit MCP Security & Blast Radius report.
Antivirus / EDR configuration report for developer workstations.
recommended_actions: Implement TrustAudit runtime MCP firewall rules restricting shell and raw socket execution.
Audit package manifest for typosquatted open-source dependencies.

controls.title: Monitoring of Configuration Changes and Susceptibility to Newly Discovered Vulnerabilities
controls.description: The entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in the introduction of new vulnerabilities, and (2) susceptibilities to newly discovered vulnerabilities.
controls.rationale: 69 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are automated dependency vulnerability scans executed on every pull request and continuous build?
Is there a formal Service Level Agreement (SLA) for patching critical vulnerabilities (e.g. 7 days for CRITICAL)?
Does the team monitor CISA KEV or national vulnerability databases for actively exploited component vulnerabilities?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit Dependency & SBOM Scan report.
Vulnerability Patching Policy document specifying remediation timelines by severity.
Pull Request / CI security gate build logs.
recommended_actions: Configure automated Dependabot / Renovate / TrustAudit CI security checks.
Upgrade dependencies with known high-severity CVEs.

controls.title: Authorized Change Management & CI/CD Security Gates
controls.description: The entity authorizes, designs, tests, approves, and documents changes to infrastructure, applications, and configurations prior to production deployment.
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Are direct commits to the production branch blocked via branch protection rules?
Is peer code review required and enforced before merging code changes?
Are automated security tests and regression tests required to pass before deployment?
evidence_requirements: GitHub / GitLab branch protection rule settings screenshot.
CI/CD workflow pipeline definition file (`.github/workflows/*.yml`).
Sample Pull Request showing peer approval and automated security check pass.
recommended_actions: Wire TrustAudit CI quality gate (`ci_scan.py`) into GitHub Actions pipeline.
Enforce minimum 1 peer code review on all pull requests.

metadata.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (including AMD 1:2024 Climate action)
metadata.authority: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) / International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)
metadata.description: Global Information Security Management System (ISMS) standard prescribing organizational, people, physical, and technological security controls.
metadata.disclaimer: TrustAudit evaluates technical control posture across selected Annex A controls. Automated technical scans do not establish full ISMS conformity or accredited ISO 27001 certification, which requires accredited third-party certification body audits.

controls.title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities
controls.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use shall be obtained, the organization's exposure evaluated, and appropriate measures taken to address the associated risk.
controls.rationale: 69 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Does the organization conduct continuous static and dynamic vulnerability assessments across all production assets?
Are vulnerabilities prioritized based on exploitability, threat intelligence (CISA KEV), and asset criticality?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit Comprehensive Security Audit Report.
Documented Vulnerability Management Procedure.
recommended_actions: Establish weekly continuous monitoring scans across repositories and public web assets.
Maintain remediation tracking SLA for critical and high findings.

controls.title: Networks Security
controls.description: Networks and network devices shall be secured, managed, and controlled to protect the information in systems and applications.
controls.rationale: 31 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are public perimeter web servers hardened against cross-origin data theft (CORS) and clickjacking?
Are network-exposed services authenticated with zero unauthenticated remote procedure calls?
evidence_requirements: Perimeter network security scan report.
Firewall & CORS configuration review.
recommended_actions: Replace wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with specific trusted origin allowlists.
Ensure MCP servers with network transports enforce bearer token authentication.

controls.title: Use of Cryptography
controls.description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, shall be defined and implemented.
controls.rationale: 26 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Is deprecated cryptography (TLS 1.0/1.1, MD5, SHA-1) phased out across all application endpoints?
Are cryptographic API keys and private keys protected against source code repository leakage?
evidence_requirements: TrustAudit TLS Configuration & Cryptographic Analysis report.
Secret detection zero-leakage scan verification.
recommended_actions: Enforce TLS 1.2+ minimum and disable obsolete legacy cipher suites.
Rotate any secrets previously committed to git history.

controls.title: Secure Development Life Cycle
controls.description: Rules for the secure development of software and systems shall be established and applied to developments within the organization.
controls.rationale: 135 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are security requirements identified and addressed across all phases of the software development lifecycle?
Are automated security gates enforced in continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines?
evidence_requirements: Documented Secure Software Development Life Cycle (S-SDLC) policy.
CI/CD build pipeline logs demonstrating automated security testing gates.
recommended_actions: Formalize an S-SDLC policy incorporating automated static analysis and vulnerability scans.
Enforce branch protection rules and automated security gate passing before production deployment.

controls.title: Secure Coding
controls.description: Secure coding principles shall be applied to software development.
controls.rationale: 135 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Are developers provided with secure coding guidelines addressing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities?
Are static code analysis (SAST) checks automated before merging code into production?
evidence_requirements: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) build reports.
Secure Coding Policy and developer training records.
recommended_actions: Remediate command injection, SQL injection, and path traversal vectors identified in SAST audit.
Implement parameterization and parameterized database query builders.

metadata.name: General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
metadata.authority: European Data Protection Board (EDPB) & National Data Protection Authorities
metadata.description: Regulation protecting fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons regarding the processing of personal data and free movement of such data.
metadata.disclaimer: TrustAudit provides automated technical control checks and record-keeping tools. Statutory compliance remains the legal responsibility of the Data Controller.

controls.title: Data Protection by Design and by Default
controls.description: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures, such as pseudonymisation, designed to implement data-protection principles effectively and integrate necessary safeguards into processing.
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Are privacy-enhancing measures (least privilege, tenant isolation, pseudonymization) designed into application schemas?
Are default settings configured to collect only personal data necessary for each specific purpose?
evidence_requirements: Architectural Data Flow Diagram (DFD) and schema design review.
Multi-tenancy isolation audit report.
recommended_actions: Isolate tenant databases or apply Row-Level Security (RLS) on personal data tables.
Disable default telemetry tracking on user sessions.

controls.title: Security of Processing (Technical & Organizational Measures)
controls.description: Taking into account the state of the art, costs of implementation, and nature of processing, the controller and processor shall implement technical measures including encryption, integrity, confidentiality, and regular testing of security effectiveness.
controls.rationale: 57 active security finding(s) directly threaten this control. See remediation center.
assessment_questions: Is personal data encrypted both in transit and at rest using modern encryption standards?
Does the organization have a process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of technical measures?
evidence_requirements: Regular automated vulnerability scanning and code audit reports.
Encryption in transit and at rest configuration verification.
recommended_actions: Run periodic automated SAST and DAST scans with verified audit trail records.
Enforce HTTPS with secure cookie attributes (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`).

controls.title: Notification of a Personal Data Breach to Supervisory Authority
controls.description: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the competent supervisory authority.
controls.rationale: This is a governance or legal control that cannot be validated purely via technical scans. Supporting documentation and legal sign-off required.
assessment_questions: Does your Incident Response procedure mandate 72-hour formal notification to the relevant Lead Supervisory Authority?
Are security incidents logged in an immutable audit trail?
evidence_requirements: Documented Data Breach Notification Procedure with 72-hour timeline.
Incident triage log template.
recommended_actions: Configure immediate automated alerts for detected credential exposures or perimeter breaches.
Maintain contact channels with the designated European Data Protection Authority.
